svg.title: How vertices and edges are built from the layout
svg.desc: Animated schematic of W8 and its four Pecos neighbours: one vertex per node and heading, translation edges that keep the heading and need both nodes to allow it, rotation edges only at W8 because only W8 has rotation_allowed, the motion type of each edge, and a route that needs two rotations; beside the abridged constructors of PoseGraph and GarageGraph.
svg.metadata: ["The layout part. W8 and its four neighbours (schematic, not to scale) with the four YAML edges between them. The edges are undirected and know nothing about headings. W8 lists headings [0\u00b0, 90\u00b0] and rotation_allowed: true; W31, W9, W4 and W13 list [90\u00b0] and may not rotate. Their other edges are not drawn.", "Vertices. GetAllowedHeadings adds the reciprocal of every listed heading, and PoseGraph makes one pose per (node, heading), in node-id order. W8 gets four poses, each neighbour two. GarageGraph adds one vertex per pose in the same order, so the vertex number is the pose index: (W8, 90\u00b0) is v16. The tick on each circle is where the AGV faces.", "Translation rule, shown for (W8, 90\u00b0). For each layout neighbour, PoseGraph builds the pose with the same heading, (Wn, 90\u00b0), and keeps the edge only if that pose exists. All four neighbours allow 90\u00b0, so v16 gets four translation edges. A translation never changes the heading: the AGV moves without turning.", "Which slot each edge is stored in. The slot comes from the edge's bearing minus the heading taken as a math angle, which is a quarter turn off the AGV's own frame. The AGV at (W8, 90\u00b0) faces west: W31 is its forward (slot LEFT), W9 its back (RIGHT), W13 its right (FORWARD) and W4 its left (BACK).", "The same rule for every pose. The 90\u00b0 vertices form one layer and the \u221290\u00b0 vertices another; each layout edge gives one directed edge each way in each layer: 4 layout edges \u00d7 2 headings \u00d7 2 directions = 16 translation edges in this sketch. Nothing connects the two layers yet.", "(W8, 0\u00b0) and (W8, 180\u00b0). The rule looks for (W31, 0\u00b0), (W9, 0\u00b0), (W13, 0\u00b0), (W4, 0\u00b0) and the 180\u00b0 equivalents, and finds none: no neighbour allows 0\u00b0 or 180\u00b0. These two vertices get no translation edge; they exist only as steps for turning.", "Rotation edges, only at nodes with rotation_allowed. Each pose of W8 links to the nearest other heading of W8 clockwise (ROT_RIGHT) and counter-clockwise (ROT_LEFT): from 90\u00b0, ROT_RIGHT is 0\u00b0 and ROT_LEFT is 180\u00b0. Four poses \u00d7 2 = 8 directed ROTATION edges, a ring that joins the two layers. The neighbours have none.", "Edge types, set by GarageGraph::AddEdge. Rotation slots become ROTATION (length: the yaw difference). A translation is typed by geometry: along the AGV's facing axis (east\u2013west here) it is LOCOMOTE, sideways (north\u2013south) STRAFE. The slot name plays no part; (W8, 90\u00b0) to (W13, 90\u00b0) is a STRAFE.", "A route that needs rotation: turn an AGV at W31 from 90\u00b0 to \u221290\u00b0. W31 cannot rotate, so the shortest route drives to W8 (LOCOMOTE, backwards), turns twice (90\u00b0 to 0\u00b0 to \u221290\u00b0) and drives back (LOCOMOTE, now forwards): v57, v16, v15, v14, v56. Through 180\u00b0 instead costs the same."]

g.text: Schematic: distances are not to scale (W8–W31 is 2.86 m, W8–W9 6.30 m, W8–W4 2.29 m, W8–W13 4.39 m). Headings, rotation flags and edges from the Pecos YAML; vertex numbers are pose indices, which equal Boost vertex indices because GarageGraph adds the vertices in pose order to a vecS adjacency_list. A

g.text: double-headed line or arc stands for two directed edges, one each way. Heading convention: 0° north, counter-clockwise, 90° faces west.

g.text: One vertex per node and heading; translation edges keep the heading and need both nodes to allow it; rotation edges stay on one node and exist only where rotation_allowed is true. Step through W8 and its four Pecos neighbours.
